blocks.value: A nested class is a class declared inside another class. The containing class is called the top-level class. There are four kinds:

- Static member class: has access to the top-level class's static methods.
- Non-static member class (inner class): requires an instance of the top-level class, and can access all its data and methods.
- Local class: defined inside a method body.
- Anonymous class: a local class with no name.
The most common reason to nest a class is that it's only ever used by its top-level class, so packaging them together keeps the connection clear.

HouseData is private here, which hides its members from anything outside RealEstateListing. An inner class can reach its top-level class's fields and methods even when they're private, and the top-level class can reach right back into its inner class too.
